intent: Commit hooks run in linked worktrees
notes: On Windows, a commit made in a linked worktree (`git worktree add`) skipped every Gator hook without an error: no charter check, no dangerous-pattern pause, no trailers (#103). Gator set a relative `core.hooksPath = .git/gator-hooks`, which Git resolves from the current worktree, where `.git` is a file. Gator now sets an absolute path to the hook folder in the Git directory that all worktrees share. The next `gator init` or `gator update` repairs existing repositories.

The hook helpers also work when run from a worktree, on every platform. Before, they treated a worktree as having no Git directory, so `gator init` reported `hooks ok` there although no hooks would run.

`gator init` now asks Git where a commit will look for hooks. If no Gator hook is there, it reports "hooks will not run here" with a `!` instead of `✓`. This also covers a clone that was moved after its hooks were installed, which the absolute path does not follow until it is repaired (Architect decision: absolute path over moving Windows to Git's default hook folder).
